aps.message: [BatteryPackConfig!B1,B11] The pack's own resistance caps electrical output at 106 kW (at I = V_oc/2R, where half the energy is burnt inside the pack). The 50 A fuse caps usable output at 23.7 kW once sag is included. Neither number appears anywhere in the workbook, and both are worth having next to the motor rating before anyone sizes a controller.

[BatteryPackConfig!B11] Pack internal resistance reads 1.7920 ohm; for 140S3P it is 0.5973 ohm. The formula multiplies the TOTAL cell count by R_cell/P, which cancels to S*R_cell and discards the parallel benefit entirely — so it is high by exactly the parallel count, 3x. This value feeds every joule-heating figure and both EMF columns, so those are all high by the same factor.

mf0_0.message: [ElecPropulsion!B2, BatteryPackConfig!B11] The motor is rated 150 kW peak. This pack cannot deliver more than 106 kW into any load, because at 0.597 ohm the maximum-power point is V_oc/2R and beyond it output falls. The motor rating is unreachable by 44 kW regardless of controller settings.

[BatteryPackConfig!B1, ElecPropulsion!B2] The 50 A fuse limits usable output to 23.7 kW with sag included, against a 150 kW motor — a factor of 6.3. Either the fuse is sized for a much smaller envelope than the motor, or the motor is specified far above what the car will ever use. Both are defensible; having neither written down next to the other is not.
